recall_prompt: Say how you would find the conjugate of this product — what you do first, and what a conjugate changes.
insider_note: Multiply first and take the conjugate last — the conjugate needs the product written as one number a + ib. Both real contributions are negative here, −8 and 30i² = −30, so the real part is −38; the conjugate then changes only the sign of the i part.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply out
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both real parts and the i² term are negative here, so the real part is −8 − 30 = −38. Watch the signs on every product.
steps.memory_tip: 30i² = −30, so the real part is −8 − 30 = −38. Both real contributions are negative here.

recall.must_convey: That the product is expanded and simplified with i² = −1 to −38 − 8i.

steps.why: The conjugate acts on one number a + ib, so the product must be simplified to that shape first. Here 30i² = −30 is the term most often mis-signed.

steps.label: Take the conjugate
steps.memory_tip: Keep the real part, flip only the i term: −38 − 8i becomes −38 + 8i.
lines: The conjugate of a + ib is a − ib.

recall.must_convey: That the conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part, so the conjugate of −38 − 8i is −38 + 8i.

steps.why: Only the imaginary part changes sign under conjugation. The real part −38 is negative and stays negative — a negative real part is not a reason to flip it.
